item.title: ¡Que Viva Antonio Aguilar! Pepe Aguilar Talks Tribute Album to His Father Featuring Ángela Aguilar, Carín León & More
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to this special edition of our podcast, where we dive into the latest music trends. Today, we're celebrating the legacy of Mexican music legend Antonio Aguilar, courtesy of his son Pepe Aguilar. Get ready to experience the iconic songs of Antonio Aguilar like never before.
[Music transition]
Host: Pepe Aguilar has just produced a compilation album, ¡Que Viva Antonio Aguilar!, featuring 14 reimagined tracks by stars from various generations. The album includes performances by Banda El Recodo, Banda MS, Carín León, and even Pepe himself, along with his children. As Pepe Aguilar shares, "It's a very special album... a record like this of Antonio Aguilar has never been done before."
[Short music clip plays]
Host: The album, set to release on May 28th under Equinoccio Records/Virgin Music, boasts an impressive lineup. Ángela Aguilar and Leonardo Aguilar perform "China de los Ojos Negros" and "El Adolorido," respectively, while Pepe Aguilar sings "Noches Tenebrosas." Other notable artists include Lucero, Guadalupe Pineda, and even a non-Mexican artist, Jessi Uribe.
[Music transition]
Host: What's particularly special about this album is the inclusion of the late Vicente Fernández, a close friend of Antonio Aguilar's. Pepe Aguilar explains that the idea to include Don Vicente came from his wife, and it's a beautiful tribute to their friendship.
[Short music clip plays]
Host: Antonio Aguilar, born on May 17, 1919, was a cultural and musical icon of Mexico, with over 150 recorded albums and hits like "Un Puño de Tierra" and "Caballo Prieto Azabache." Known as "The Charro of Mexico," he was also a prominent figure in Mexican cinema, appearing in over 160 films.
[Music transition]
Host: Pepe Aguilar shares his admiration for his father's career, saying, "He was a proud Mexican who loved his homeland and traditions." This compilation album is a testament to Antonio Aguilar's enduring legacy, and we can't wait to experience it.
[Outro music plays]
Host: Thanks for tuning in to this special episode. ¡Que Viva Antonio Aguilar! is set to release on May 28th, so mark your calendars and get ready to celebrate the music of a Mexican legend. Until next time, adiós!
